transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, what brings me in is... I just keep getting these awful doubts that I've missed something important. It could be a number on the mortgage payment, a clause in a client proof for work, or even just a door not being latched. 

And the thing is, even when I know I checked it, the thought just barges right back in. It's always something like, "What if this is the mistake that costs you everything?" It's just become really hard to deal with.
Do you find yourself doing anything over and over to try to get rid of these doubts?

Yes, I do. I end up reopening files, rereading emails... checking the online payment confirmation over and over. Sometimes I just say the figures silently in my head until they finally feel settled. It takes up so much time. What should be a simple invoice or a basic logo revision can easily turn into hours of extra work, and it's time that I just can't bill for.
Do you feel anxious when you're not thinking about these doubts or checking things?

No, not really. I mean... if I'm actually not thinking about them, I feel fine. It's not like I'm just walking around feeling nervous all day for no reason. 

The anxiety really only hits when one of those doubts pops into my head, or... or if I'm trying to force myself not to go back and check something. But if I'm just going about my day and my mind is actually clear of all that? No, I don't think I feel anxious then.
Do you find yourself performing any physical actions repeatedly, like touching or tapping, in response to these doubts?

No, I don't really do anything like that. I don't tap things or, you know, touch things a certain number of times. It's really just the checking... going back to look at the screen or the paper, or just going over the numbers in my head. But no physical habits like tapping.
Are these doubts and the time you spend checking things interfering with your relationships or daily life in any significant way?

Yes, it definitely is. It's really affecting my work. I mean, I've actually missed billable hours because of this. And I've had to push back deadlines... work that used to take me an afternoon now drags on for days because I'm stuck checking everything. It's getting to the point where one of my longtime clients actually questioned whether I can still handle simple revisions on time. So, yes, it's definitely causing a problem.
How distressed do you feel when these doubts and the need to check things are at their worst?

I'm not really sure how to measure it, to be honest. I mean... it's just incredibly frustrating. When it's at its worst and I'm just stuck checking the same design file over and over, I feel very tense and... just really annoyed with myself. 

I wouldn't say I'm having a complete breakdown or anything, but it's a very uncomfortable, trapped kind of feeling. I don't know if that's exactly what you mean by distressed, but that's what it feels like to me.
Do you have any recurring thoughts or images that aren't about checking things, but still feel intrusive or unwanted?

No, not really. It's really just the checking. I don't have any other thoughts or images popping into my head that bother me. It's just that constant nagging feeling that I've made a mistake in my work and need to look at it again.
Have you started avoiding certain tasks or situations because of these doubts and the need to check things?

No, I haven't really avoided anything. I mean, I still do all my work and take on the same types of projects. I just end up spending way too much time on them because of all the checking. But I don't avoid the work itself.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and feel intrusive or unwanted, aside from these doubts about mistakes?

No, I think we just covered that, actually. Like I said a moment ago, it's really just the work stuff. I don't get any other kinds of repeating thoughts or images or anything like that. Just the constant worry that I messed up a design file and need to check it again.
Are these doubts and checking habits affecting your personal relationships or leisure activities in any way?

Well, it's not so much my personal relationships or free time, but it's definitely affecting my business. I'm a graphic designer, and... well, I've missed billable hours because of this. I've had to push back deadlines. A project that used to take me an afternoon now drags on for days because I'm just checking and rechecking the files. It's gotten to the point where one of my longtime clients actually asked me if I could still handle simple revisions on time. That was pretty hard to hear.
Are you feeling like these doubts and checking habits are affecting your overall well-being or ability to function in daily life beyond the impact on your work?

Not really, no. I mean... like I mentioned, it's really just tied to my work. When I'm not at my desk, I'm fine. I can run errands, do things around the house, and just go about my day normally. It doesn't really spill over into my regular routine, aside from just the general stress of knowing I'm falling behind on my projects. But my actual ability to function outside of work is perfectly fine.
Are you feeling like these doubts and checking habits are affecting your relationships with family or friends?

No, like I think I mentioned a minute ago, my relationships are fine. It hasn't caused any problems with my family or my friends. When I'm not at my computer working, I'm... I'm just not doing the checking. So it doesn't get in the way of spending time with them or anything like that.
Are you feeling like these doubts and checking habits are making it difficult for you to enjoy things you normally like to do?

No, not really. I mean, I still enjoy my hobbies and doing things in my free time. The only thing is, sometimes it's hard to fully relax because I'm stressed about the work I'm behind on. But the checking itself doesn't stop me from enjoying a book or going for a walk, it's just the stress from work that kind of hangs over me.
Would you say that the frustration and tension you feel from these doubts and checking habits are overwhelming at times?

I wouldn't say overwhelming, no. I mean... it's definitely frustrating. Sitting there checking the same design file over and over makes me tense, sure, because I know I'm wasting time. But it doesn't completely overwhelm me. It's really just that... that underlying stress of being behind on my work, rather than feeling like I can't handle it at all.
Would you describe the feelings of frustration and tension from these doubts and checking habits as distressing to you?

I don't know if I would use the word distressing. Um... it's definitely annoying. I get mad at myself for wasting time when I have design deadlines to meet, but... distressing sounds a bit too severe to me. It's really just that frustration of knowing I'm slowing myself down and making my own job harder.
